description.value: The study investigated FDG-PET metabolic connectivity and resting-state network alterations in frontal and temporo-limbic variants of behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia using SICE and seed-based IRCA analyses.

spans.text: we combined two different multivariate analytical approaches, i.e., the sparse inverse covariance estimation (SICE) method for the evaluation of whole-brain metabolic connectivity ( ) and seed-based interregional correlation analyses (IRCA) for assessing the resting-state networks integrity ( )

value: We hypothesised distinct alterations both in whole-brain metabolic connectivity and in the resting-state networks, contributing to the clinical phenotypes of the two variants, which are mainly characterised by executive deficits in the frontal variant and poor long memory performance in the temporo-limbic patients
